headline: GOLD RALLIES 1.1% TO $4,163 AS PHYSICAL BUYERS RETURN — OIL ABOVE $100 AND IRAN STRAIT DEADLOCK CLOUD THE BOUNCE
snippet: Gold surged 1.14% to $4,162.84/oz on September 29 as physical buyers re-entered the market following Monday's eight-week low, with BullionVault noting steady coin and bar demand across physical desks. The recovery faces a ceiling: Brent crude remains above $100/bbl after Washington rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, keeping inflation fears alive and 70% of futures markets pricing in an October Fed rate hike. Silver lagged, rising just 0.11% to $61.05/oz. For junior gold mining investors, the $4,100-$4,163 range has emerged as the critical near-term battleground — a sustained close below $4,100 would open the technical door to the 50-day moving average near $4,050 and materially compress developer project economics.

headline: GEOINTELX + SEG LAUNCH AI PLATFORM QUERYING 100 YEARS OF GEOLOGICAL DATA — DRAW A MAP, TARGET A DEPOSIT IN MINUTES
snippet: GeoIntelX announced September 29 a strategic partnership with the Society of Economic Geologists (SEG) that integrates more than 100 years of peer-reviewed publications, geological maps, and datasets into the GIX AI geospatial platform. Geoscientists can now delineate a region of interest on a map, query trained AI agents with complex geological questions, and receive contextual answers fusing SEG's century-long scientific archive with public datasets and a company's own proprietary exploration data. For junior mining companies, this is the first time academic economic geology — including analogue deposit research — is queryable in a spatial context without specialist expertise. The partnership is expected to compress the cycle from data collection to drill-hole prioritisation and lower the cost of greenfield targeting.

headline: GOLDEN CARIBOO INAUGURAL NI 43-101 RESOURCE: 175K OZ INDICATED + 995K OZ INFERRED AT QUESNELLE BC — MAIN ZONE NOT YET INCLUDED
snippet: Golden Cariboo Resources announced its inaugural NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate on September 29 for the past-producing Quesnelle Gold Quartz Mine Property in central British Columbia: 10 million tonnes at 0.55 g/t Au for 175,000 indicated ounces, plus 70.9 million tonnes at 0.44 g/t Au for 995,000 inferred ounces of gold, based on 24 diamond drill holes totalling 8,466 metres. The estimate covers only the Halo and North Hixon zones — the Quesnelle Main Zone, which hosts six additional company holes plus historical surface drill data, is excluded from this resource and represents future upside. For retail investors tracking BC gold juniors, the inaugural resource establishes a NI 43-101 baseline that can be built on; the fact that the bulk-mining grade system remains open beyond the 24-hole database suggests further resource growth is the primary near-term thesis.

headline: MONTAGE GOLD POURS 1,140 OZ AT KONÉ AHEAD OF SCHEDULE — CÔTE D'IVOIRE MINE ENTERS OXIDE PRODUCTION, HARD ROCK CIRCUIT FOLLOWS Q2 2027
snippet: Montage Gold Corp. (TSX: MAU) achieved first gold pour at its flagship Koné mine in Côte d'Ivoire on September 26, yielding approximately 1,140 ounces on budget and ahead of the original schedule, following ore introduction into the oxide circuit on September 8. More than 400,000 tonnes of ore have been processed since commissioning, and the oxide circuit is targeting commercial production in Q4 2026, with the hard-rock comminution circuit remaining on budget for completion in Q2 2027. Koné is now Côte d'Ivoire's ninth operating gold mine. For context: Montage Gold ranked second overall in the 2026 TSX30, which measures three-year dividend-adjusted performance, reflecting the market's recognition of the project's development trajectory before this milestone was reached.

headline: WGC: CHINA'S PEAK GOLD SEASON STARTS OCT 1 — PBOC ON 22-MONTH BUYING STREAK AS GOLDEN WEEK SETS DIRECTION FOR Q4
snippet: The World Gold Council's September 28 Weekly Markets Monitor, titled 'Golden Week in China,' highlights that the October 1-7 National Day holiday traditionally marks the start of China's peak gold-buying season — bringing stronger jewellery sales, trade restocking and firmer local premiums. The People's Bank of China added 20.2 tonnes in August, its largest single-month purchase since October 2023, extending official buying to 22 consecutive months and pushing total reserves to 2,387 tonnes (9% of total FX reserves). China's gold imports are tracking toward 1,200 tonnes for 2026, which would be a record annual figure. The WGC cautions that elevated gold prices above $4,000/oz and subdued Chinese consumer confidence have dampened jewellery demand, suggesting Q4 physical demand will be more investment-driven than the seasonal tradition implies.

headline: CATL'S BIGGEST LITHIUM MINE LOSES EIA — BENCHMARK SLASHES 2026 JIANXIAWO OUTPUT FORECAST 49% TO 32,000T LCE
snippet: China's largest lithium mine by planned capacity — CATL's Jianxiawo lepidolite operation in Jiangxi — is back in care and maintenance after regulators revoked its Environmental Impact Assessment in early September 2026, following a brief unauthorised restart in July that triggered more than 70 formal complaints over an unresolved tailings pond dispute. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence has cut its 2026 mined output forecast for the mine from 62,500 tonnes LCE to 32,000 tonnes — a 49% reduction — while a sustained restart requires completing a full environmental review that could extend into Q4 2026 or 2027. Lithium carbonate in China was trading at 123,400 CNY/T on September 29, down 2.33% on the day and 22% over the past month, despite the Jianxiawo supply disruption — reflecting how the market is still working through existing inventory rather than the longer-term structural tightening this shutdown implies.

headline: CRITICAL METALS TANBREEZ +25%, USA RARE EARTH +6%: US-GREENLAND SECURITY PACT PUTS ARCTIC REE PERMITS IN PLAY
snippet: A new US-Denmark-Greenland security arrangement signed in September 2026 catalysed a rare earth equity rally: Critical Metals (NASDAQ: CRML), which owns the Tanbreez Rare Earth Project in southern Greenland, surged 25% on September 21 as investors priced in an accelerated path to permitting. USA Rare Earth added 6%, MP Materials rose 4%, and TMC The Metals Company climbed 9.5%. Critical Metals gained a further 9% on September 24 as the agreement's details emerged, underscoring that the Greenland story is an ongoing catalyst rather than a one-day trade. The deal is part of a broader Trump administration strategy of taking equity stakes in Western-aligned rare earth miners to reduce dependence on China, which controls more than 60% of global rare earth processing capacity.

headline: URANIUM TERM/SPOT SPREAD HITS $11 — $91.50 CONTRACTS VS $89 SPOT SIGNALS STRUCTURAL DEFICIT UTILITIES SEE COMING
snippet: Long-term uranium contract prices rose to $91.50/lb while spot traded near $89/lb — an $11 term premium that Crux Investor argues is a forward signal from utilities locked into multi-year supply agreements who anticipate a coming deficit before spot buyers see it. Global uranium production stands at approximately 150 million pounds annually against nuclear utility demand of roughly 200 million pounds; the 50-million-pound gap is being met by drawing down secondary inventories. Kazatomprom — the world's largest producer — cut 2026 production guidance by roughly 10%, choosing not to sell at current prices rather than indicating weak demand. A sulphuric acid plant failure at a Saskatchewan processing facility also halted the McArthur River mine for 12 days, highlighting how concentrated Western uranium supply chain risk remains around a small number of processing nodes.

headline: CHINA GOLD IMPORTS TRACKING RECORD 1,200T IN 2026 AS PHYSICAL DEMAND OFFSETS JEWELLERY SLUMP
snippet: China's gold imports are on track to approach 1,200 tonnes for all of 2026, which would represent a new annual record, driven by a combination of sustained People's Bank of China official purchases, firm local premiums in Shanghai, and rising investment demand that is more than offsetting the weakness in retail jewellery sales caused by elevated gold prices and subdued consumer confidence. The structural demand picture supports the gold bull thesis: even with Chinese jewellery demand impacted by gold prices above A$6,500/oz equivalent, investment-channel and central-bank demand in China is absorbing supply and firming local premiums. For junior gold mining investors, China remaining a structural buyer at record pace — even as Western markets price in October rate hikes — is a key pillar of the medium-term supply-demand balance.
